title: Louis Armstrong, Emmett Harding and Bix Beiderbecke in New Orleans
summary: He remembers Louis with King Oliver, the young cornetist Emmett Harding, a steamboat cutting contest, and his belief that Bix took his style from Harding; also Kid Rena.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Mm-hm. well they called them cafes in them days, on Rampart Street. Him and King Oliver was playing together. Loey was playing the second trumpet. I never will forget that. And I was just starting out and I heard so much about Loey. And I went in there and heard him playing. And then in later years after he got playing good there, there was a little boy come up there by the name of Emmett Harding. He was very good. And Emmett was playing with a band by the name of Brownlee, who was a bass player. And Brownlee was playing at a hall they called the Owl's Hall. They used to play all around too. In those days the bands would go from corner to corner playing. I could see this little boy setting on top of the piano, playing his cornet with his half a pint on the side of him. And I mean, he would make a variation front ways and turn around and play that thing backwards and man, that's as good as he played in front. That's how good he was now. And then in later years, him and Loey got hooked up on a steamboat out there. I think it was a steamer capital or a sydney. I don't know which one. I think it was a sydney myself. And Loey was on one end. He was playing with Fate Marvel, I think. I think he was playing with Fate. And this Brownlee band was on the other end. And I think Monk Hazel played in that band too with him. And then Loey started blowing at this boy. And this boy was mad. This boy started blowing back at him. And Loey bowed to him and said, Brother, you can play. And he says, You're better mad than I am. But the kid died young. And in the meantime, this is when Bix Spider-Bike came down here. And this kid taught Bix what he knew. And Bix to me took his style because this kid played two styles. He played the style Bix played and he played the style Loey played. And Bix was down here doing nothing. And he took this style back up north and made a lot of money with it. That's what I think about that kid. It was the most outstanding trumpet player down here at that time. Let it years and years come along like Red Bone was a fine trumpet band too. And different one, there was a colored boy there that played plenty trumpet down here too. He's dead and that's kid, Rene. And I say he could play as much trumpet as what Loey played. In fact, he played pretty Loey in those days.
